_comment: Emerging / scaling brands. momentum 1-5 (5 = scaling hardest right now). threat = how directly it competes with a premium soap/scent/body proposition. Update signals as you find them; the news collector will also surface mentions automatically.

watchlist.name: Flamingo Estate
watchlist.why: Took luxury soap/candle pricing in under five years on pure narrative — agricultural provenance, produce-to-product. Wholesale into premium grocery and design retail, not beauty.
watchlist.watch: Whether it holds price as distribution widens.

watchlist.name: TAMBURINS
watchlist.why: Gentle Monster's retail-theatre playbook applied to hand cream. Sculptural packaging turned a commodity format into a collectible.
watchlist.watch: Western wholesale entry — would land directly on Byredo/Diptyque hand cream.

watchlist.name: NONFICTION
watchlist.why: Seoul minimal-luxury positioning hand cream as fragrance layering. Scaling into EU/US concept and department stores.
watchlist.watch: Which EU doors it wins — same buyers as Aesop and Le Labo.

watchlist.name: Nécessaire
watchlist.why: Defined body-skinification. Ingredient-percentage marketing at roughly half the luxury body price undercuts the fragrance-led premium.
signals: Category extension into hair and deodorant
watchlist.watch: Whether skinification claims keep beating scent equity with under-35s.

watchlist.name: Cyklar
watchlist.why: Named by BoF among indie brands to watch in 2026 in body care.
watchlist.watch: Retail wins and funding — verify details before quoting.

watchlist.name: Hanni
watchlist.why: Took investment from L'Oréal's venture arm — a strategic signal that big beauty sees premium body care as the growth pocket.
watchlist.watch: Whether L'Oréal scales it against Nécessaire.

watchlist.name: Xinu
watchlist.why: Latin American niche perfumery gaining international editorial traction; strong object/packaging design.

watchlist.name: Fugazzi
watchlist.why: Fast-rising niche fragrance house with a distinctive counter-culture voice.

watchlist.name: Vyrao
watchlist.why: Energy/wellness framing of fragrance; strong UK department-store traction.

watchlist.name: Ffern
watchlist.why: Ledger/waitlist model — seasonal batches, no retail, no discounting. The most interesting scarcity mechanic in scent right now.
watchlist.watch: Model is highly transferable to candles and soap — worth studying regardless of category.

watchlist.name: Haeckels
watchlist.why: Radical-transparency and regenerative-packaging comms; B-Corp. Sets the bar for credible sustainability claims.
watchlist.watch: The claims playbook to benchmark yours against.

watchlist.name: Corpus Naturals
watchlist.why: Design-forward natural body care with strong concept-store distribution — same doors as Tangent GC.

watchlist.name: Sangre de Fruta
watchlist.why: Botanical luxury with a distinctive romantic visual language; strong in independent luxury retail.

watchlist.name: Binu Binu
watchlist.why: Korean bathhouse-inspired artisan soap. Small but a reference point for narrative-led bar soap.

watchlist.name: Moëhr
watchlist.why: Gourmand-led niche perfumery riding the haute-cuisine scent trend.

watchlist.name: Keap Candles
watchlist.why: Coconut-wax DTC candle with a clean-burn/transparency angle at half the luxury price.

watchlist.name: Maison Balzac
watchlist.why: Glassware-first house where the vessel is the product. Strong design-retail and gifting position.
watchlist.watch: Vessel-as-object is the same lever Astier and L'OBJET pull.
